transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love anymore, even painting or going to my dance class. My husband and a close friend from my walking group noticed how much I've pulled back, and they persuaded me to come in today.
Did these changes start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they seem to come on without a clear trigger? About how long have you been feeling this way?

This all really started to take hold about four months ago. It seemed to trigger after my youngest daughter moved several hours away for a new job, and around the same time the community center cut back on the senior arts programs I loved. Since then, I've just felt so heavy and empty inside.

Before these past four months, have you ever had another period lasting at least a couple of weeks when you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things? If so, did it happen without a clear stressful event?
No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before these past few months. This is the very first time I've experienced such a severe change and felt so empty inside.

Over these past two weeks, have you been feeling down or hopeless most of the day nearly every day, even when you’re not thinking about your daughter moving or the program cuts? Or does the sadness mainly come up when you think about those losses?

Yes, I feel this heavy, sad feeling almost every single day now, pretty much all day long. Even when I'm not thinking about my daughter or the center, I wake up with this hollow feeling in my chest and just start crying over nothing in particular. It just doesn't seem to lift.
Over the past two weeks, have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt? If so, which ones have been happening nearly every day?

Yes, my energy is completely gone, and even simple things like getting dressed or making breakfast wear me out so much that I have to sit right back down. I also feel like a useless burden to my family nearly every day, and I blame myself for everyone drifting away. I haven't really noticed changes in my sleep, appetite, or concentration, though.

How much is this affecting your daily functioning—are you still able to manage basic chores, self-care, and social activities, or have you largely stopped doing them because of how depressed you feel?

It has completely taken over my life, and I've stopped going to church, the senior center, and my dance group altogether. Most days, my husband has to nudge me just to bathe or cook because I feel so useless. Even getting dressed or making a simple breakfast wears me out so much that I have to sit right back down.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life? If yes, have you had any plan or intent to act on those thoughts?

Yes, I sadly have had those thoughts, and I sometimes think it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I've even pictured taking all of my blood pressure pills at once. I haven't actually tried to do anything, though.

When something positive happens, like time with family or a pleasant activity, does your mood noticeably lift even for a little while, or do you still feel depressed almost the same? Has there been any time in the past month when you felt close to your usual self for a day or two?

No, my mood doesn't lift at all, and interacting with my family actually makes me feel worse because of this constant fear that they are distancing themselves—sometimes I even hear my daughter's voice saying cruel things. I haven't had a single day in the past month where I felt close to my usual self, as this heavy, empty feeling has been completely constant for the last four months.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime episode of a severe depressive syndrome lasting about 4 months, with persistent depressed mood and marked anhedonia plus low energy, excessive guilt/worthlessness, major functional decline, and suicidal ideation with a contemplated overdose method. Psychotic features are present, as the patient reports hearing her daughter's voice saying cruel things in the context of depression. Symptoms are pervasive, not limited to thinking about the stressors, and exceed what would be expected for adjustment disorder or uncomplicated bereavement.
